title: Small Compiler Subset BSharp VM Execution Independence
purpose: Give BSharp Compiler Subset 0 its own bounded BSBC execution engine for Profiles 1 through 7 while preserving the production BytecodeVirtualMachine and BasicSharp::Runtime only as separate referees for exact execution meaning.

allowed: adding compiler/small_compiler_subset_bsbc_virtual_machine.rb as the independent Subset 0 execution engine
executing models validated by SmallCompilerSubsetBSBCLoader without requiring, inheriting from, or calling the production BytecodeVirtualMachine
using compiler/bytecode_virtual_machine.rb only on a separate production-VM referee path
using BasicSharp::Runtime as the Ruby meaning referee
requiring exact START, event matching, Kind inheritance, selector, action ordering, object interaction, value mutation, IF/OTHERWISE, follow-up event, loop-protection, final-world, and Save parity
running high-volume deterministic event parity on the dedicated v0.0.77 fixture
proving Profile 1 through Profile 7 execution without changing bytecode layout or creator-facing meaning
forbidden_until_later_approval: inheriting SmallCompilerSubsetBSBCVirtualMachine from the production BytecodeVirtualMachine
routing normal BASIC# production execution through the subset VM
retiring the Ruby bootstrap compiler or Ruby runtime referee

fixture.name: v077_independent_bsbc_vm_execution
required_features: open close lock take object interaction

acceptance_rules: SmallCompilerSubsetBSBCVirtualMachine must not require, instantiate, inherit from, or call the production BytecodeVirtualMachine.
The production BytecodeVirtualMachine may remain loaded only for a separate referee comparison.
The Ruby BasicSharp::Runtime remains a separate semantic referee.
Dedicated fixture event results, final world, and BSharp Save document must match both referees.
The independent VM must still execute when the production BytecodeVirtualMachine constructor is disabled.
High-volume execution must remain deterministic across 1,024 events and match the production VM and Ruby referee semantics.
No Profile 8, binary-format change, full self-hosting claim, or Ruby retirement is allowed.
